title: Sharps
summary: Black keys can be named after the white key to their left, with a sharp.

steps.title: Sharp
steps.body:
A black key can take its name from the white key on its left. **Sharp** means one key higher, to the right. Its sign is ♯. The black key just to the right of C is **C sharp**, written C♯.

**Why it matters:** Bands use sharps all the time: a song in F♯, a C♯ in the bass line. With sharps you can find every black key by name.

steps.title: Signs that move a note
steps.body:
A sign that moves a note up or down from its plain letter is called an **accidental**. The ♯ sign is the first one you know, and the next two lessons add two more.

**Why it matters:** When you see a sign next to a note name on a chart or in a chord name, it is an accidental. It tells you to play a neighbouring key instead of the plain white key.

steps.title: The five sharps
steps.body: From the left: C♯, D♯, F♯, G♯ and A♯. Each is just to the right of the white key it is named after.

items.prompt: Play F#: find F, then go one key to the right.

steps.title: Black keys by name
steps.body: Play each black key and say its sharp name out loud. The app shows the name, so you can check.
